nutshell: Tech Rally Reignited Amid AI Investment Frenzy

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: This is the February 9th market close briefing. Today, we saw a strong rally with both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq hitting new all-time highs. It looks like the market's heating up again.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. Today's market can be summed up as 'a tech rally reignited by the AI investment frenzy.' The S&P 500 gained 0.47% to close at 6964.82, breaking the 6900 level for the first time ever. The tech-heavy Nasdaq also hit a new record, climbing 0.9% to 23238.67. In contrast, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was relatively sluggish, up just 0.04%. This is because the market's momentum was really concentrated on major investment news related to artificial intelligence. Specifically, news that Alphabet is set to issue $20 billion in bonds to expand its AI data centers was a powerful driver for investor sentiment.

sources.title: Alphabet Set to Raise $20 Billion From US Dollar Bond Sale

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So Alphabet's massive fundraising has really boosted expectations for the entire AI sector. This seems to be about more than just one company's news.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Exactly. The market interpreted this as a signal of structural growth across the entire AI industry. Morgan Stanley noted that the tech rally could run further, with AI supporting solid revenue outlooks. And we're seeing huge amounts of capital flowing into the AI ecosystem, with private AI firm Databricks, for example, being valued at $134 billion. You could say this 'AI gold rush' phenomenon is what drove today's tech-led rally.

sources.title: Morgan Stanley’s Wilson Says Tech Rally Can Run Further on AI
Databricks valued at $134 billion in $5 billion fundraise, CNBC reports

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: I see. So, could you break down the key market drivers for us today, including this 'AI gold rush' you mentioned?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Certainly. Two main themes drove the market today. First, how the 'AI gold rush' we just discussed fueled the broader tech rally. And second, how software stocks, which recently pulled back on fears that AI could be a threat, managed to bounce back. Let's take a closer look at each of these.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Alright, let's start with the AI gold rush. Just how significant was the scale and impact of the capital flowing into the AI space?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Well, today the market was completely dominated by a massive wave of capital pouring into AI. The fact that the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both hit all-time highs while the Dow remained flat clearly shows how concentrated the momentum was in AI-related tech stocks. The epicenter of this frenzy was the news that Alphabet's $20 billion bond sale for AI data centers attracted a record-breaking $100 billion in orders. And this isn't just a public market story. The private data software company Databricks raised $5 billion, valuing it at $134 billion. This flow of funds lifted the entire semiconductor sector, with the SOXX ETF gaining over 1.2%. On top of that, a weaker dollar created a favorable environment for tech stocks with high overseas sales. This combination of factors is precisely why Morgan Stanley believes the AI-led rally can continue.

sources.title: Alphabet Set to Raise $20 Billion From US Dollar Bond Sale
Databricks valued at $134 billion in $5 billion fundraise, CNBC reports
Morgan Stanley’s Wilson Says Tech Rally Can Run Further on AI

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So this astronomical amount of money is flowing into actual AI infrastructure—physical assets like data centers and semiconductors. I imagine the companies providing the 'picks and shovels' for this gold rush were also quite active.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's exactly right. The focus of investment is shifting from simple hype to actual infrastructure build-out. A prime example is the Australian AI infrastructure developer Firmus, which announced it secured $10 billion from firms like Blackstone to build data centers based on Nvidia's hardware. Nvidia, the leading AI chipmaker, saw its stock rise 2.5% today, validating market expectations. This trend is spreading throughout the supply chain. Marvell Technology, which manufactures Amazon's custom AI chip, Trainium, also climbed over 2.5%, boosted by Amazon's massive AI investments. It's gotten to the point where even Elon Musk's xAI is reportedly seeking a $3.4 billion loan from Apollo Global Management to buy Nvidia chips. The competition to secure AI computing power is truly heating up into a full-blown war.

sources.title: Australian AI infrastructure developer Firmus lands $10 billion debt package from Blackstone, Coatue

Apollo, xAI near $3.4 billion deal to fund AI chips, the Information reports

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: With such a huge amount of capital flowing into just one specific area, doesn't this create market imbalances or raise concerns about overheating?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, and that's another key aspect to watch. This isn't a market where anything with an 'AI' label gets a free pass. We're seeing some speculative behavior, like the domain name ai.com selling for a record $70 million. But the market is gradually starting to separate the wheat from the chaff. Recently, some software stocks fell sharply on concerns that new AI tools could disrupt their business models. Even giants aren't immune; despite its massive fundraising news, Alphabet's stock actually slipped slightly today amid issues like a trademark lawsuit with Autodesk over AI software. This shows that even within the AI theme, stock performance is starting to diverge based on specific business models and competitive strengths.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: I see. So you're saying that while the AI rally continues, a sorting process has begun within it. So, what would you say is the most important trend we saw in the market today?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: The key takeaway is that the grand narrative of AI is now driving the market to a new level through tangible capital investment and infrastructure build-out. Confidence in the companies that enable and deploy AI technology remains solid, as shown by Microsoft, which led the rally today with a gain of over 3%. Morgan Stanley's analysis suggests that the value of not only the enablers of AI but also the companies that adopt it for innovation is not yet fully priced into the market. The fact that the broader tech ETF, XLK, rose over 1.5% is evidence of this. The 10-year Treasury yield also helped, slipping slightly and providing a stable backdrop for this growth-stock rally. Ultimately, the market is betting on the structural changes AI will bring, and it has begun the journey of identifying the real winners who will lead that change.

sources.title: Morgan Stanley’s Wilson Says Tech Rally Can Run Further on AI

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: As you said, there were some interesting moves as the market searches for those 'real winners.' You mentioned earlier that software stocks, which were seen as being threatened by AI, bounced back strongly today. How should we interpret that?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, that was the most telling subplot of the day. While the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were hitting record highs, the 10-year Treasury yield remained stable below 4.2%, and the VIX, the volatility index, dropped over 14%, signaling clear risk-on sentiment across the market. But one sector that had been left out of this rally was software. It was facing what some called a 'SaaSpocalypse,' the fear that AI agents would destroy existing subscription models. However, today the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF surged over 3%, successfully reversing the mood. This can be attributed to a strong wave of bargain hunting as fears about AI were seen as overblown, all happening amid a stable macro environment with a weaker U.S. dollar and oil prices rising above $64 a barrel.

sources.title: US software stocks tumble sparks concerns that AI trade is reshaping markets
ZoomInfo, DigitalOcean, Fastly, Samsara, and SoundHound AI Shares Are Soaring, What You Need To Know

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: 'SaaSpocalypse'—so it was serious enough to be called the end of Software-as-a-Service. What was the key reason for such a dramatic turnaround in just one day?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: You could say that rational counterarguments prevailed after the fear reached its peak. The recent sell-off was triggered by concerns that new AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic could replace existing software. However, sentiment recovered quickly after reports from investment banks like Barclays argued that it would take years for companies to switch systems, meaning the economic moats of established leaders remain intact. The view that AI will be an augmenting factor—improving efficiency by integrating into existing software, as seen with ServiceNow or GitLab—gained traction over the idea that it would be purely destructive. In fact, ServiceNow rose over 3% today, and the SKYY cloud computing ETF also gained nearly 2%, reflecting this shift in thinking.

sources.title: ZoomInfo, DigitalOcean, Fastly, Samsara, and SoundHound AI Shares Are Soaring, What You Need To Know
US software stocks tumble sparks concerns that AI trade is reshaping markets

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So, can we say that investors decided AI is more of an opportunity than an immediate threat, and used the recent dip as a buying opportunity?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Precisely. The market saw this as opportunistic buying of quality stocks that had entered oversold territory. We saw a particularly strong rebound in stocks that had fallen the most. Data analytics firm Samsara jumped over 7% in a single day, while sales intelligence platform ZoomInfo and financial automation software company Bill.com also led the rebound, each gaining 3.7%. Cloud infrastructure provider DigitalOcean was up nearly 3% as well. Ironically, the companies hit hardest by the AI threat narrative were the ones at the forefront of today's rally. This shows a consensus formed among market participants that the short-term stock decline was excessive compared to the long-term changes AI will bring.

sources.title: ZoomInfo, DigitalOcean, Fastly, Samsara, and SoundHound AI Shares Are Soaring, What You Need To Know

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Do you think today's strong rebound could be more than just a one-day event and turn into a trend? What's the outlook for the software sector going forward?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: It's still too early to be complacent. Today's rebound was a result of extreme pessimism subsiding, but the underlying uncertainty from the AI-driven shift hasn't disappeared. In fact, for the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF, implied volatility in the options market—which bets on future price swings—remains high, and short interest is also at unusually high levels. This suggests the tug-of-war between bulls and bears over the future of the software industry will continue for some time. Ultimately, it seems only the companies that can prove they can successfully integrate AI into their services to create new value will earn the market's trust and join the current tech rally.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Okay, so a sorting process has begun within the massive AI trend. Now, let's take a closer look at some noteworthy individual company moves. First up is Goldman Sachs. It gained 1.57% today to close at $943.61, showing strong momentum after hitting a high of $949 during the session.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, despite today's stock price increase, Goldman Sachs is internally facing a stark contrast between its future growth potential and its current financial risks. It seems the market's attention is focused on an innovative narrative that views Goldman not just as an investment bank, but as a tech company providing financial infrastructure. There's a lot of hope that its new 'Platform Solutions' division will lead to a re-evaluation of the company's value. But on the flip side, this new business is generating massive losses, and the company is also carrying the heavy burden of legacy legal risks. This has sparked a fierce debate about whether the current stock price adequately reflects these dangers.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: And this 'Platform Solutions' you mentioned—that's the growth engine that's supposed to turn Goldman into the Amazon Web Services of finance, right?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. From a positive perspective, this division is seen as a bold R&D investment for the future. In fact, the net revenue of the Platform Solutions segment has grown by over 60% in just two years, showing rapid expansion on the surface. Furthermore, the move to step back from consumer finance, such as selling the GM credit card business, is viewed by some as a smart strategic shift to exit low-margin, high-risk areas and focus on a high-return B2B platform. From this viewpoint, the current losses are a necessary step to secure future market dominance, and some analysts suggest that the market's pessimism is excessive, potentially creating a good entry point.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: The future growth potential is very interesting, but what's the specific level of risk we're talking about right now?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: And that's exactly where a cautious approach is warranted. According to the 2025 10-K filing, the Platform Solutions division, touted as the growth engine, has recorded a staggering cumulative loss of about $5.2 billion over the past three years. This has led to criticism that it's not an investment in the future, but a cash-burning business that is seriously eroding shareholder value. On top of that, the company is exposed to potential additional legal losses of about $1.7 billion, exceeding its current reserves, due to various lawsuits related to events like the SVB collapse and the Archegos scandal. This is a potential risk not yet fully reflected on the balance sheet, which, if realized, could directly impact the company's net income and shareholder value.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So it's basically a tug-of-war between a rosy future vision and billions of dollars in real-world losses.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Exactly. Right now, Goldman Sachs is using profits from its strong traditional businesses to cover the losses from its new ventures. The problem is that the success of these new ventures is still uncertain, and it's hard to find precedents of a large bank successfully transforming into an agile tech company. The current stock price appears to be weighing the potential for future success more heavily than the significant execution risks and ongoing financial losses. Therefore, considering the impact of proven risk factors like the Platform Solutions losses and the $1.7 billion contingent liability on the company's intrinsic value, risk management seems prudent at the current valuation level.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Well, it was a historic week with the S&P 500 crossing the 5,000 mark. Looking ahead, what should we be watching to gauge the market's next move?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, as you mentioned, the S&P 500 showed incredible strength, crossing 5,000 for the first time ever. This was driven by solid corporate earnings and optimism about AI. But whether this positive mood will continue depends on the upcoming economic data. In particular, all eyes are on next week's inflation reports, as they will be the most critical clues for determining the timing and extent of the Fed's rate cuts.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: When you say next week's inflation data, you're talking about the CPI, the Consumer Price Index, right?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. The January Consumer Price Index, or CPI, will be released next Tuesday, the 13th. While the market expects the year-over-year inflation rate to have slowed, a hotter-than-expected number could cause expectations for an early rate cut to retreat significantly. With Fed officials recently showing a cautious stance on rate cuts, this CPI report will be a crucial turning point for the market's short-term direction. Investors may need to prepare for increased volatility.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Are there any other important dates to watch after the CPI release?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Absolutely. After the market digests the CPI, it will look for more details on the Fed's thinking. On the 18th, the minutes from the January Federal Open Market Committee, or FOMC, meeting will be released. These minutes could reveal subtle differences in opinion among the members about the timing of rate cuts and the depth of their discussions. Then, on the 20th, we'll get the Personal Consumption Expenditures, or PCE, price index, which is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge. These two events should give us a clearer picture of the Fed's policy path.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So, after hitting an all-time high, the market is now facing a major hurdle in the form of inflation data. That's all for our February 9th market close briefing. Thank you.
